title: O God! I Thank Thee That the Night
description: O God! I Thank Thee That the Night in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: John Pierpont wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 366, “Morning Hymn for a Child”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O God! I thank Thee that the night In peace and rest hath passed a-way, And that I see in this fair light My Fa-ther's smile, that makes it day.

lines: O God! I thank Thee that the night
In peace and rest hath passed away,
And that I see in this fair light
My Father's smile, that makes it day.
Be Thou my guide, and let me live
Supply my wants, my sins forgive,
And make me happy when I die.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Pierpont died in 1866.
credits: Words by John Pierpont (1785–1866), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
